summary: Teams of 2-4 students create a 3-5 minute podcast episode exploring myths and realities about teenagers and technology. The podcast must address two specific myths, use real-world evidence, demonstrate effective audio production, and include a clear takeaway message. Teams submit their podcast and supporting documents before the deadline and present their work to judges at the competition.
time_limits: Setup: no more than three (3) minutes
Presentation: no more than ten (10) minutes
Judges’ questions: no more than five (5) minutes
submission_requirements: Submit one combined PDF file containing clickable URL to Podcast, Works Cited, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form
Upload completed projects to a video/file sharing link (Vimeo, YouTube, Dropbox, etc.)
Projects must be viewable on Windows and Mac platforms
Set the access level of your project to one of BPA’s recommended settings
Team ID is required for all submissions
Materials from non-registered contestants and/or those missing Team ID cannot be accepted
Secure a signed BPA Release Form(s) from any person, including themselves, whose image or work is used in the project
Cite all sources, including oneself, on the Works Cited page for any work used on the project
Materials must follow BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization’s name
deadlines: National Deadline: April 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
what_to_bring: One single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for presentation
competencies: Apply audience analysis and design principles & elements to research and develop discussion points, outlines, and scripts, ensuring clear messaging and engagement for a defined target audience across platforms

Develop and edit professional lead-in and lead-out segways and implement audio editing and splicing workflows using industry-standard software, incorporating nonlinear editing, mixing, and effects to enhance storytelling and production value

Utilize industry-standard audio production software, hardware, and workflows and apply modern recording techniques to capture clear, high-quality sound in various environments, adapting to project needs and technical requirements
Collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary audio production teams, utilizing project management and communication platforms to optimize workflow and production quality

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy.

Team submitted one (1) combined PDF file containing clickable URL to Podcast, Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form.
Topic addressed with multiple actors and viewpoints
Podcast made effective use of time and was within the audio time limit of 3-5 minutes

rubric.description: Catchy, clever intro with relevant info and a clear purpose that engages the listener right away.
Creative, original content supports the podcast’s purpose. Information is accurate.
The podcast is presented in highly engaging, conversational way that draws the listener in.
Music enhances the podcast, suits the mood and content. Volume is well-balanced and clear.
Delivery is well-rehearsed & smooth. The speaker enunciates clearly & uses an appropriate expression.

rubric.criterion: Use of Ambient Sound & Noise Control
rubric.description: Podcast has zero to very minimal background noise and/or interruptions.

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Team maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and varies their tone and pace adequately.
Presentation content flows adequately, and each team member's role is clear and integrated into the presentation. Transitions between speakers and/or points are smooth.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.
Setup lasted no longer than three (3) minutes, and the presentation lasted no more than ten (10) minutes.

judging_notes: Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the team within the time allotted
No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, contestants may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
No materials may be left with the judges
Only the team captain should complete the submission
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this judged team event
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants
Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy will be disqualified
AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
